title: Cases: An Overview
explanation: German has four cases (Nominativ, Akkusativ, Dativ, Genitiv) that change articles and adjective endings depending on a noun's role in the sentence - subject, direct object, indirect object, or possession.

examples.text: Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch.

title: Gender of Nouns: der / die / das
explanation: Every German noun has one of three genders - masculine (der), feminine (die), or neuter (das) - and this must usually be memorized with each noun.

title: Present Tense Regular Verbs
explanation: Regular verbs drop the -en/-n ending and add: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en for ich/du/er-sie-es/wir/ihr/sie.

examples.text: machen -> ich mache, du machst, er macht
wir machen, ihr macht, sie machen

title: Word Order: Verb-Second
explanation: In a main clause, the conjugated verb is always the second element - not necessarily the second word - even if the sentence starts with something other than the subject.
